title: Nonperturbative Infrared Behavior of Nonamenable Sigma Models
exact_target: Determine rigorously whether noncompact sigma models really have the long-distance behavior predicted by perturbation theory.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 30000464 (OWR-1266-002). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.
The Rigorous Renormalization Group (2006), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2006/17, pp. 1027--1076; official report source and mathematical context.
Official EMS Press PDF of the same Oberwolfach report; PDF pages 15 and 42--43, printed pages 1041 and 1068--1069.

status_qualification: There is a provenance mismatch: the supplied original excerpt is the functional-integral problem from Niedermaier's warped-product, dimensionally reduced gravity contribution, whereas the clean statement uses the infrared question in Seiler's separate nonamenable-target contribution. They must not be silently identified. The catalogue clean formulation is retained and both source targets are distinguished.
